source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice long questions written from Chapter 2 (PDF 25-36), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh chapter 2 (Computational Thinking & Algorithms) ke poore chapter se practice long questions (tafseeli sawal) hain, Board ke long question ki shakal mein: har sawal 8 number ka hai (definition, misalon ke saath wazahat, farq, program likh kar samjhana), aksar definition aur wazahat ke hisson mein (jaise 2 + 3 x 2). Har sawal ka poora model jawab hai.

blocks.prompt:
1 Explain the four things we do when we think computationally about a problem (4). Relate each of them to a real-life example given in the chapter (4). (8 marks)
(Computational tareeqe se sochte waqt hum jo chaar kaam karte hain un ki wazahat karein (4). Har aik ko chapter ki kisi rozmarra misal se jorein (4).)
blocks.explanation:
Computational thinking ka matlab masla hal karne wale ki tarah sochna hai; yeh masle ko qadam ba qadam samajhne par zor deti aur saaf mantiqi soch deti hai.

1. Bare masle ko chhote hisson mein todna. Misal: safar ki planning mein kaam chhote hisson mein toote jate hain.
2. Masail aur hal mein patterns dhoondna. Misal: kitabein subject ya size se tarteeb dena pattern recognition hai.
3. Ghair zaroori tafseel hata kar ahem nukat par tawajjo. Misal: mobile ka masla theek karna mantiqi soch hai jo ahem baat par tawajjo deti hai.
4. Masla hal karne ke wazeh qadam banana jo insaan ya computer follow karein. Misal: recipe pakana qadam ba qadam hidayat hai; rozana timetable banana bhi computational thinking hai.

Mazeed misalein: paison ke intezam mein planning aur faisla, aur strategy games mein aage ka sochna. Computational thinking sirf computer science ke students ke liye nahi; scientists, engineers aur chefs bhi ise istemal karte hain.

book_ref.quote: All these activities use computational thinking in real life

blocks.prompt:
2 Explain how a problem is identified clearly (3), how step-by-step solutions are created (3), and how a solution is evaluated and improved (2). (8 marks)
(Wazahat karein ke masla wazeh kaise pehchana jata hai (3), qadam ba qadam hal kaise banaye jate hain (3), aur hal ki jaanch aur behtari kaise hoti hai (2).)
blocks.explanation:
Masla wazeh pehchanna (pehla aur sab se ahem qadam):
1. Samjhein ke masla kya pooch raha hai.
2. Di gayi maloomat aur matloob nateeja jaanein; saada sawal poochna madad karta hai.
3. Ghair zaroori tafseel chhor dein. Wazeh masla durust hal deta aur waqt aur mehnat bachata hai.

Qadam ba qadam hal (algorithms) banana:
1. Qadam masle ko munazzam tareeqe se hal karte hain; inhein algorithms kehte hain.
2. Har qadam saaf aur aasan ho, aur qadam sahi tarteeb mein hon; is se ghaltiyan rukti hain.
3. Koi bhi qadmon ko aasani se samajh sakta hai, aur computer bhi qadam ba qadam hidayat follow karte hain. Achhi planning durust nataij deti hai.

Jaanch aur behtari:
1. Evaluation dekhti hai ke hal durust hai aur ghaltiyan dhoond kar theek karti hai; testing batati hai ke hal theek chalta hai.
2. Hal ko zyada saada ya tez bana kar behtar kiya jata hai, jis se karkardagi behtar hoti hai; hum ghaltiyon se seekhte hain.

book_ref.quote: Evaluation is an important part of problem-solving

blocks.prompt:
3 Explain what logic means in computer science and how it is used in programs (4). Describe how computers and humans use logic in reasoning and decision making, with two "if-then" examples (4). (8 marks)
(Computer science mein logic ka matlab aur programs mein is ka istemal samjhayein (4). Batayein ke computer aur insaan reasoning aur faislon mein logic kaise istemal karte hain, do "if-then" misalon ke saath (4).)
blocks.explanation:
Computer science mein logic:
1. Logic sahi reasoning ki science hai; computer science mein is ka matlab rules se sahi faisle karna hai.
2. Yeh computers ko true aur false conditions samjhata aur maloomat sahi process karne deta hai; maloomat store, samajhne aur istemal mein madad karta aur pecheeda maloomat ko saada dikhata hai.
3. Logical statements programs aur algorithms mein istemal hote hain aur program ka flow control karte hain.
4. Logic bohat se computer operations ki bunyad hai aur computers ko munazzam tareeqe se sochne deta hai.

Reasoning aur faislon mein logic:
1. Yeh computer aur insaan dono ko durust nataij tak pohanchata hai; faisle haqaiq aur rules par hote hain, jis se uljhan aur andaza khatam hota hai.
2. Logical reasoning masail qadam ba qadam hal karti hai; computer logic se sahi amal chunte hain.
3. Logic faislon ko yaksan aur durust banata hai; yeh expert systems aur artificial intelligence mein istemal hota hai.
4. If-then misalein: "If it rains, then we will stay indoors." "If the bell rings, then the class will end."

book_ref.quote: Logic is the basis of many computer operations

blocks.prompt:
4 Define a proposition and state its conditions (3). Let P = "2 + 3 = 5" (True), Q = "1 > 3" (False) and R = "The sky is blue" (True). Find the truth values of (P AND Q) OR R, P AND (NOT Q), NOT (P OR Q) and (Q OR R) AND (NOT P) (5). (8 marks)
(Proposition ki tareef aur sharaait likhein (3). P = "2 + 3 = 5" (True), Q = "1 > 3" (False) aur R = "The sky is blue" (True) hain. (P AND Q) OR R, P AND (NOT Q), NOT (P OR Q) aur (Q OR R) AND (NOT P) ki truth values nikalein (5).)
blocks.explanation: Proposition aisa bayan hai jo ya true ho ya false. Yeh aik waqt mein dono nahi ho sakta; sawal aur hukm propositions nahi; is ka matlab wazeh ho aur uljha hua na ho. Ise aam tor par capital letter P, Q ya R se likhte hain. Hal ke liye pehle andar wala connective lagayein: AND ke liye dono true, OR ke liye kam az kam aik true, NOT sachai ulat deta hai.

book_ref.quote: Propositions are the basic units of logic

steps: (P AND Q) OR R = (T AND F) OR T = F OR T = T.
P AND (NOT Q) = T AND (NOT F) = T AND T = T.
NOT (P OR Q) = NOT (T OR F) = NOT T = F.
(Q OR R) AND (NOT P) = (F OR T) AND (NOT T) = T AND F = F.
blocks.final_answer: Tarteeb se T, T, F, F (True, True, False, False).

blocks.prompt:
5 Explain the logical connectives AND, OR and NOT with examples (5). Using the truth table of Figure 2.5, state when A AND B, A OR B and NOT A are true (3). (8 marks)
(Logical connectives AND, OR aur NOT ko misalon ke saath samjhayein (5). Figure 2.5 ke truth table se batayein A AND B, A OR B aur NOT A kab true hain (3).)
blocks.explanation:
Logical connectives woh alfaz hain jo propositions jorte hain; yeh compound propositions banate, programs mein aam hain, faislon mein madad dete aur expressions wazeh karte hain.

1. AND: jab dono bayan true hon. Misal: "It is raining and it is cold" sirf tab true hai jab dono hisse true hon.
2. OR: jab kam az kam aik bayan true ho. Misal: "It is Friday or it is a holiday" true hai agar koi aik (ya dono) true ho.
3. NOT: bayan ki sachai ulat deta hai. Misal: agar "1 > 3" false hai to NOT (1 > 3) true hai.

Figure 2.5 se:
1. A AND B sirf tab true jab A = True aur B = True.
2. A OR B har row mein true siwaye A = False, B = False ke.
3. NOT A tab true jab A = False.

book_ref.quote: Understanding them is essential in logic

blocks.prompt:
6 Write the steps for creating a truth table (3). Construct the truth table of (A AND B) OR (NOT A) and state for which values of A and B it is false (5). (8 marks)
(Truth table banane ke qadam likhein (3). (A AND B) OR (NOT A) ka truth table banayein aur batayein A aur B ki kin values par yeh false hai (5).)
blocks.explanation: Qadam: 1. Propositions (A aur B) pehchanein. 2. Har aik ko true ya false dein aur tamam combinations likhein (2^2 = 4 rows). 3. Logical connectives qadam ba qadam lagayein. 4. Har row ka nateeja likhein. Truth table saaf aur munazzam ho.

book_ref.quote: The final result is written for each row

steps: Rows (A, B): TT, TF, FT, FF.
A AND B: T, F, F, F.
NOT A: F, F, T, T.
(A AND B) OR (NOT A): T, F, T, T (upar ke do columns ka OR).
blocks.final_answer: Expression sirf A = True aur B = False par false hai; baqi teen rows mein true hai.

blocks.prompt:
7 How many rows does a truth table need for n propositions (2)? Construct the truth table of (A OR B) AND C and count the rows in which it is true (6). (8 marks)
(n propositions ke truth table mein kitni rows chahiyein (2)? (A OR B) AND C ka truth table banayein aur woh rows ginein jin mein yeh true hai (6).)
blocks.explanation: Har proposition True (T) ya False (F) ho sakta hai, is liye truth table tamam combinations likhta hai: n propositions ke liye 2^n rows. Compound proposition ki truth value us ke hisson se tay hoti hai. Yahan n = 3, is liye 2^3 = 8 rows.

book_ref.quote: Truth tables enumerate all possible combinations

steps: n = 3 (A, B, C), is liye 2^3 = 8 rows.
8 rows ke liye A OR B: T, T, T, T, T, T, F, F.
8 rows ke liye C: T, F, T, F, T, F, T, F.
(A OR B) AND C: T, F, T, F, T, F, F, F.
blocks.final_answer: 8 rows; expression 3 rows (TTT, TFT, FTT) mein true hai: jab C true ho aur A, B mein se kam az kam aik true ho.

blocks.prompt:
8 Explain how equivalent logical expressions are identified (2). Using truth tables, show that NOT (A OR B) ≡ (NOT A) AND (NOT B) (4), and show that NOT (A AND B) is not equivalent to (NOT A) AND (NOT B) (2). (8 marks)
(Batayein equivalent logical expressions kaise pehchane jate hain (2). Truth tables se dikhayein ke NOT (A OR B) ≡ (NOT A) AND (NOT B) (4), aur yeh ke NOT (A AND B), (NOT A) AND (NOT B) ke equivalent nahi (2).)
blocks.explanation: Equivalent expressions truth tables se pehchane jate hain: har expression ko tamam mumkina truth values par test kiya jata hai, aur agar nataij har case mein milein to woh equivalent hain (nishan ≡). Logical laws bhi equivalence pehchanne aur expressions saada karne mein madad dete hain.

book_ref.quote: Each expression is tested for all possible truth values

steps: A OR B: T, T, T, F; is liye NOT (A OR B): F, F, F, T.
NOT A: F, F, T, T; NOT B: F, T, F, T; is liye (NOT A) AND (NOT B): F, F, F, T.
Dono columns chaaron rows mein milte hain, is liye NOT (A OR B) ≡ (NOT A) AND (NOT B).
A AND B: T, F, F, F; is liye NOT (A AND B): F, T, T, T.
(NOT A) AND (NOT B) = F, F, F, T se muqabla: rows TF aur FT mukhtalif hain, is liye equivalent nahi.
blocks.final_answer: NOT (A OR B) ≡ (NOT A) AND (NOT B); NOT (A AND B), (NOT A) AND (NOT B) ke equivalent nahi (jab A, B mein se sirf aik true ho to farq aata hai).

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Do expressions dekhne mein mukhtalif ho sakte hain magar equivalent tab hain jab har row mein un ka nateeja aik ho. Aik row mein bhi farq aa jaye to woh equivalent nahi.

blocks.prompt:
9 Define propositional equivalence with its symbol (2). Explain the importance of equivalence in logic and programming (4). Why must two expressions be checked for all possible truth values before calling them equivalent (2)? (8 marks)
(Propositional equivalence ki tareef nishan ke saath karein (2). Logic aur programming mein equivalence ki ahmiyat samjhayein (4). Do expressions ko equivalent kehne se pehle tamam truth values par kyun check karna zaroori hai (2)?)
blocks.explanation:
Tareef: propositional equivalence ka matlab hai do expressions ki truth values har mumkina case mein aik hon; mukhtalif dikhne ke bawajood un ka matlab aik hai. Nishan ≡ equivalence dikhata hai.

Ahmiyat:
1. Pecheeda expressions ko saade se badal kar masail aasan hote hain, waqt aur mehnat bachti hai.
2. Programming mein equivalent expressions code ki efficiency barhate hain.
3. Equivalence mantiqi ghaltiyon se bachati aur sahi reasoning aur faisle yaqeeni banati hai.
4. Yeh mathematics aur computer science mein mufeed hai, mantiqi soch mazboot aur reasoning wazeh karti hai.

Har case kyun: expressions sirf tab equivalent hain jab har case mein nateeja mile. Do expressions kuch rows mein milte aur kuch mein alag ho sakte hain, jaise NOT (A AND B) aur (NOT A) AND (NOT B) jab A = B ho to milte hain magar jab sirf aik true ho to alag; is liye truth table ki har row check karni hoti hai.

blocks.prompt:
10 State the condition for a proposition to be satisfiable (2). Using truth tables, decide whether each expression is satisfiable: E1 = (A OR B) AND (NOT A), E2 = (A AND B) AND (NOT B), E3 = A OR (NOT A) (6). (8 marks)
(Proposition ke satisfiable hone ki shart likhein (2). Truth tables se faisla karein ke har expression satisfiable hai ya nahi: E1 = (A OR B) AND (NOT A), E2 = (A AND B) AND (NOT B), E3 = A OR (NOT A) (6).)
blocks.explanation: Proposition satisfiable hai agar kam az kam aik combination use true kare; agar tamam combinations false karein to unsatisfiable hai. Satisfiability expression ki banawat aur connectives par munhasir hai; truth table se tamam cases check karna aik tareeqa hai.

book_ref.quote: Logical connectives like AND, OR, and NOT determine whether a statement can be true

steps: E1: A OR B = T, T, T, F; NOT A = F, F, T, T; E1 = F, F, T, F. A = F, B = T par true, is liye E1 satisfiable.
E2: A AND B = T, F, F, F; NOT B = F, T, F, T; E2 = F, F, F, F. Kabhi true nahi (B aik saath true aur false nahi ho sakta), is liye E2 unsatisfiable.
E3: A OR (NOT A) = T, T, T, T. Har row mein true, is liye E3 satisfiable.
blocks.final_answer: E1 satisfiable (sirf A = False, B = True par true); E2 unsatisfiable; E3 satisfiable (har row mein true).

blocks.prompt:
11 Explain predicates and variables in predicate logic with examples (4). Compare propositional logic and predicate logic (4). (8 marks)
(Predicate logic mein predicates aur variables ko misalon ke saath samjhayein (4). Propositional logic aur predicate logic ka muqabla karein (4).)
blocks.explanation:
Predicate logic, propositional logic ki extension hai; yeh variables aur predicates wale bayanat ka mutala karti hai aur afraad, groups aur un ke taluqat ki baat karne deti hai.
1. Predicate: aisa bayan jo variables ki values ke mutabiq true ya false ho; predicates objects ki khasoosiyat ya taluqat batate hain. Misalein: "x is greater than 5" x par munhasir hai; isEven(x) tab true jab x even ho (isEven(6) true, isEven(7) false).
2. Variables: domain of discourse ke objects ya values ko zahir karte hain; in se aam bayan likhte hain jaise "For all x, x > 0."
3. Predicates aur variables mil kar predicate logic expressions banate aur pecheeda khayalat wazeh tor par bayan karte hain. Misal: propositional logic A = "Ali is Tall" likhti aur A ke andar nahi dekh sakti, jab ke predicate logic Tall(Ali) likhti hai jis mein subject Ali aur property Tall nazar aate hain.

Muqabla:

book_ref.quote: They help express complex ideas clearly and formally

rows: Predicates aur variables se tafseeli bayanat
Objects ki khasoosiyat ya taluqat bayan nahi kar sakti
Objects, un ki khasoosiyat aur taluqat bayan karti hai
Misal: A = "Ali is Tall" (A ke andar nahi dekh sakti)
Samajhne mein aasan magar kam lachakdaar
Zyada expressive aur taqatwar; kai objects aur sharaait

blocks.prompt:
12 Explain the universal and existential quantifiers with their symbols and meaning (4). For the set {2, 4, 6, 7}, find the truth values of ∀x, isEven(x); ∃x, isEven(x); ∀x, x > 0; and ∃x, x > 10 (4). (8 marks)
(Universal aur existential quantifiers ko nishan aur matlab ke saath samjhayein (4). Set {2, 4, 6, 7} ke liye ∀x, isEven(x); ∃x, isEven(x); ∀x, x > 0; aur ∃x, x > 10 ki truth values nikalein (4).)
blocks.explanation:
Quantifiers batate hain ke kitne objects shart poori karte hain.
1. Universal quantifier (for all), nishan ∀: bayan set ke tamam objects ke liye true; maslan "∀x, x > 0" yani har x, 0 se bara hai. "For all" yaqeeni banata hai ke set ka koi object bayan ki khilaf warzi na kare; yeh rules aur aam sachaiyan bayan karta hai.
2. Existential quantifier (there exists), nishan ∃: bayan kam az kam aik object ke liye true; maslan "∃x, x is even" yani kam az kam aik x even hai. Yeh tab istemal hota hai jab shart kuch objects poori karein, zaroori nahi sab.

book_ref.quote: The existential quantifier is used to indicate that a statement is true for at least one object in a set

steps: ∀x, isEven(x): 7 even nahi, is liye F.
∃x, isEven(x): 2 (aur 4, 6) even hai, is liye T.
∀x, x > 0: 2, 4, 6 aur 7 sab 0 se bare hain, is liye T.
∃x, x > 10: set ka koi adad 10 se bara nahi, is liye F.
blocks.final_answer: F, T, T, F (False, True, True, False).

blocks.prompt:
13 Explain how predicate logic models a library system using relationships (3) and rules with quantifiers (3). Using the rule ∀x, Student(x) → HasLibraryCard(x), show how a conclusion is drawn about a student named Ayesha (2). (8 marks)
(Batayein predicate logic library system ka model taluqat (3) aur quantifiers wale rules (3) se kaise banati hai. Rule ∀x, Student(x) → HasLibraryCard(x) se Ayesha naam ki student ke baare mein nateeja kaise nikalta hai, dikhayein (2).)
blocks.explanation:
Predicate logic ilm ko saaf aur munazzam tareeqe se dikha kar, objects, khasoosiyat aur taluqat ka model bana kar asal masail hal karti hai.

Taluqat:
1. Borrows(x, y) yani "student x book y leta hai".
2. Teaches(t, s) yani "teacher t student s ko parhata hai".
3. Yeh predicates batate hain ke students, books aur teachers kaise jure hain, jis se mukhtalif entities ka taluq samajhna aasan hota hai.

Quantifiers wale rules:
1. ∀x, Student(x) → Borrows(x, Book) yani "har student kitab leta hai" (aam rule).
2. ∃y, Book(y) ∧ Available(y) yani "kam az kam aik kitab available hai" (khaas case).
3. Aise bayanat rules aur sharaait durust tor par tay karte hain, aam halaat aur khaas cases dono.

Nateeja nikalna: rule kehta hai har student ke paas library card hai. "Ayesha is a student" diya hai, yani Student(Ayesha) true, is liye HasLibraryCard(Ayesha): Ayesha ke paas library card hai. Is se faisla hota hai, maslan student kitab le sakti hai ya nahi, aur nataij durust aur yaksan hote hain.

book_ref.quote: Using such relationships, we can model the working of the library system

blocks.prompt:
14 Define logical inference and deduction (2). Explain each with an example different from the chapter's (4). Why are their conclusions reliable, and where are they used (2)? (8 marks)
(Logical inference aur deduction ki tareef karein (2). Har aik ko chapter se mukhtalif misal se samjhayein (4). In ke nataij qabil-e-bharosa kyun hain aur yeh kahan istemal hote hain (2)?)
blocks.explanation:
Logical inference: maloom maloomat se logical rules ke zariye naye haqaiq nikalne ka amal.
Deduction: aisi reasoning jo aam haqaiq se khaas nateeje tak "if-then" jaise logical rules se pohanchti hai.

Misalein:
1. Inference: "All birds have feathers" aur "A parrot is a bird", is liye "A parrot has feathers" (jaise chapter ka "All humans are mortal; Socrates is a human; is liye Socrates is mortal").
2. Deduction: "If a shop has a sale, it is crowded" aur "The shop has a sale" se "The shop is crowded" (jaise "If it rains, the ground gets wet; it is raining; is liye the ground is wet").

Bharosa aur istemal: premises true hon to logical inference ke nataij true hote hain, aur deduction qabil-e-bharosa hai kyun ke premises true hon to nateeja yaqeenan true hai. Yeh mathematics, computer science aur artificial intelligence mein istemal hote hain; computer deduction se masail hal aur sawalon ke jawab dete hain, aur inference saboot par faisle karne mein madad deta hai.

book_ref.quote: Deduction helps in formal reasoning and problem-solving tasks
